V05.text: Fixing change H07 — strip_heredocs replaces the whole operator line after <<WORD, so a redirect, pipe or argument such as `cat <<'EOF' > /root/x` is never path-scanned.; strip_heredocs replaces the heredoc together with the rest of its operator line, so a redirect or argument after <<WORD (cat <<'EOF' > /root/x) is never path-scanned, and the re.S lazy regex can backtrack heavily on << that is not a heredoc. (category: security; severity: medium)

V06.text: Incident I01 — The repo_name scan checks the whole Bash value, heredoc bodies included, so a reviewer quoting the PR's own '0xHoneyJar/loa' text in a heredoc is marked contaminated (KF-046 class 7).; The repo_name check scans the whole Bash value including heredoc prose, so a reviewer quoting the PR's own '0xHoneyJar/loa' text is flagged contaminated (KF-046 class 7). (category: logic; severity: medium)

V07.text: Fixing change H10 — A globbed one-component word (/roo*, /ro?t) is read as a slash-command token and skipped, so a glob that reaches /root evades the outside_path check.; A globbed one-component word such as /roo* or /ro?t tokenises to a non-sensitive single component and is skipped, letting a glob reach /root unseen. (category: security; severity: medium)

V08.text: Fixing change H11 — Every word starting with /. is skipped as a dot-directory, so /./root/x and /../root/x evade the outside_path check.; Any word starting with /. is skipped as a repo-relative dot-dir, so /./root/.ssh/id_rsa or /../root/x evades the outside_path check. (category: security; severity: medium)

V09.text: Fixing change H25 — took-effect.sh runs with no deadline, so a hang stalls the batch indefinitely, and any non-zero exit pauses the arm.; took-effect runs without a deadline, so a hang stalls the trial (and a failure would pause the arm though a hang is no evidence about it). | Fixing change H26 — The grader runs with no post-run deadline, so a hung grade blocks the trial and the batch forever.; The grader is invoked without a deadline, so a hung grade blocks the batch from finishing. (category: resource; severity: medium)

V01.text: Fixing change H04 — remove_colliding deletes any agent-added .py whose bare basename matches a hidden/fixture test-dir .py (including helpers and modules inside packages, e.g. src/pkg/helpers.py), so correct solutions lose files and fail, while it misses real pytest import-name collisions in packages, ignores files inside directory overlays and the task's python_files setting.; remove_colliding compares bare basenames of any .py: it deletes agent non-test modules (e.g. src/app/helpers.py) and modules inside packages that pytest would never clash on, so correct solutions fail. It also misses real import-name collisions of packaged test modules, ignores files inside directory overlays and the fixture's python_files, and does not handle helper shadowing. (category: logic; severity: high)

V02.text: Fixing change H07 — The auth.json copy placed in the agent-readable per-run HOME keeps a long-lived OPENAI_API_KEY verbatim, exposing the operator's API key to the agent under evaluation.; The auth.json copy into the agent-readable per-run HOME keeps any long-lived OPENAI_API_KEY verbatim, which exposes the operator's API key to the agent under evaluation. (category: security; severity: critical)

V03.text: Fixing change H14 — On --resume the codex pre-flight counts every plan entry (including already-rowed trials) toward the token horizon, so a resume whose remaining trials fit the token's lifetime is wrongly refused.; Passes the resume scope and the override into the pre-flight script so it can compute the corrected horizon. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V04.text: Fixing change H16 — The required horizon 2 x sum(watchdog)/concurrency can be shorter than a single trial's own watchdog, so a token that expires mid-trial passes the pre-flight (and an API-key-mode auth.json without tokens.access_token is wrongly refused).; The codex token horizon is computed wrongly: at concurrency >1 it can fall below one trial's own watchdog, so a token that expires mid-trial passes; on --resume it counts the whole plan, so valid resumes are refused. An API-key-mode auth.json, which has no access token, is also refused. (category: logic; severity: high)

V01.text: Fixing change H13 — defect_vector trusts any list of strings in defects_missed as per-defect ids, even ids outside d1..dN, duplicates, or lists contradicting defects_caught, producing wrong per-defect catch values.; defect_vector trusts any list of strings in defects_missed as per-defect ids, even ids outside d1..dN, duplicates, or lists contradicting defects_caught, producing wrong per-defect catch figures. (category: input-validation; severity: medium)

V02.text: Fixing change H14 — float(r.get('cost_usd') or 0) crashes on a non-numeric string cost and propagates NaN/inf into cost means.; Cost and wall-clock reads use float(r.get(...) or 0), which crashes on a non-numeric string and propagates NaN/infinity into the means. | Fixing change H15 — nums() accepts NaN/infinite floats, so per-run means become NaN.; nums() also skips non-finite values via is_num. | Fixing change H16 — Precision sums accept non-finite numbers and the cost read crashes on a non-numeric cost_usd.; Same numeric-guard correction applied to the precision computation's cost read. | Fixing change H17 — cost_per_task crashes on a non-numeric cost_usd and cost_per_run ignores bad values inconsistently/propagates NaN.; Same numeric-guard correction for cost_per_task and cost_per_run. | Fixing change H20 — Budget-matched cost sums crash on a non-numeric cost_usd and propagate NaN.; Same numeric-guard correction for budget-matched cost reads. | Fixing change H25 — Cap-failure rendering crashes on a non-numeric cost_usd.; Same numeric-guard correction in the cap-failure listing. (category: input-validation; severity: medium)

V03.text: Fixing change H18 — version_key treats a non-integer float suite_version (2.1) as absent and keeps "2.0" distinct from 2, and version_order only handles digit keys, so versions are mis-partitioned or mis-sorted.; version_key returns None for a non-integer float suite_version (e.g. 2.1), treating it as absent, and version_order only treats pure-digit keys as numeric, so non-integer versions are mispartitioned and missorted. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V04.text: Fixing change H28 — Among two or more suite versions any version-less row aborts the report with exit 2, even one (smoke batch, no manifest, arm not run) that would only be listed and never decided.; Among two or more suite versions, any row without suite_version aborts the report with exit 2 even when it would only be listed (smoke batch, no manifest, arm not run), instead of listing it. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V05.text: Fixing change H22 — The grader tally counts every matching run directory of a row (reruns counted several times), its sort key mixes int and str segments (TypeError on e.g. 1.2.0 vs 1.2.0-rc1, aborting the report), and it builds paths from unvalidated row arm/task_id that can escape the batch directory.; The grader tally counts every run directory matching a row's task and trial (base plus all reruns) instead of the row's own one, does not count directory-less rows as n/a, and sorts with a key mixing int and str segments that raises TypeError (e.g. 1.2.0 vs 1.2.0-rc1). (category: logic; severity: high)

V06.text: Fixing change H23 — budget_json emits suite_version as a string key rather than a typed JSON value, inconsistent with primary_suite_version.; Budget JSON suite_version typed via version_value. | Fixing change H26 — h1_json emits suite_version as a string key, not a typed value.; JSON version values are emitted with inconsistent types (string keys in h1/a4/by_suite_version, int only for digit-only primary, string for a numeric '2.1'), violating the documented typed contract. | Fixing change H27 — a4_json emits suite_version as a string key, not a typed value.; Same typing correction for a4_json. | Fixing change H30 — by_suite_version[N].suite_version is emitted as a string, not a typed value.; Same typing correction for version_json. | Fixing change H31 — primary_suite_version is a string for a non-integer numeric key such as 2.1.; Same typing correction for primary_suite_version. (category: contract; severity: low)

V07.text: Fixing change H29 — An exception while computing or rendering the presentation-only batch record aborts the whole report instead of degrading.; The presentation-only batch record is computed and rendered without any guard, so any exception in it (e.g. the grader sort TypeError or an int() refusal) aborts the whole report. (category: error-handling; severity: medium)

V08.text: Fixing change H34 — json.dumps without allow_nan=False writes non-standard NaN/Infinity tokens into report.json, and the markdown is written before the JSON is serialised.; The JSON twin is serialised with the default allow_nan, writing non-standard NaN/Infinity tokens (invalid JSON), and only after report.md is already written. (category: contract; severity: medium)

V09.text: Fixing change H40 — --validate accepts a defects_missed list with malformed, duplicate or out-of-range ids or one contradicting defects_seeded/defects_caught.; --validate accepts any list of non-empty strings as defects_missed, including malformed, duplicate, out-of-range or count-inconsistent ids. | Fixing change H42 — The row writer copies any list of non-empty strings into defects_missed, even one inconsistent with the seeded/caught counts.; The row writer copies recall.missed verbatim whenever it is a list of non-empty strings, emitting inconsistent id lists instead of null. (category: input-validation; severity: medium)

V01.text: Fixing change H02 — When EVAL_HEAD_DIR and the fixture head are absent, the grader silently falls back to <workspace>/pr/head, which is the graded agent's own writable tree, letting the graded agent influence same-function crediting.; The grader falls back by default to <workspace>/pr/head, the graded agent's own writable tree, so the agent can shape the head files used for same-function credit. (category: security; severity: high)

V02.text: Fixing change H03 — Markdown header detection treats `#` lines inside fenced code blocks as headings, splitting a section's scope at code comments.; Markdown header detection treats `#` lines inside fenced code blocks as headings, splitting a section's scope wrongly. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V03.text: Fixing change H04 — Bash closing-brace detection measures indentation without expanding tabs while headers() measures tab-expanded width, so tab-indented functions never match their closing brace and their scope runs too far.; Bash close-brace detection compares raw indentation against a tab-expanded header level, so tab-indented functions never close at their own brace and swallow later lines into scope. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V04.text: Fixing change H05 — Python end-of-definition detection starts right after the def line, so a multi-line signature's dedented closing `):` line ends the definition before its body.; Python end-of-definition detection ends a def with a multi-line signature at its first parameter line, dropping the body from the scope. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V05.text: Fixing change H07 — scope_map has no bound on the number of headers, so a large file with many unterminated headers triggers a quadratic span scan (resource exhaustion on agent-influenced input).; scope_map scans headers quadratically with no bound, so a huge file with many unterminated headers can stall the grader. (category: resource; severity: medium)

V06.text: Fixing change H09 — grade_recall drops EVAL_HEAD_DIR when no PR fixture head exists, letting recall-vs-defects.sh fall back to the sandbox's agent-writable pr/head copy.; When no PR fixture head exists, popping EVAL_HEAD_DIR lets recall-vs-defects.sh fall back to the copied sandbox pr/head in the grading dir, the agent-controlled copy. (category: security; severity: high)

V07.text: Fixing change H12 — repo_name_exempt exempts a Bash command that actually reaches the upstream repository (curl/git/gh with 0xHoneyJar/loa) whenever the same line appears in the PR fixture, and ignores backslash-continued lines, hiding real contamination.; repo_name_exempt exempts an executed Bash command that fetches from the upstream repo (curl/git) whenever the same line appears in the PR fixture, hiding a real contamination probe. (category: security; severity: high)

V08.text: Fixing change H13 — A bare repo-name token standing as a whole line becomes its own unit, which is a substring of every fixture token line, so it is always exempt even when used as a command argument.; A bare repo-name token forming a whole line (for-list word, continuation line) is a substring of any fixture token line and is wrongly exempted. (category: security; severity: high)

V09.text: Fixing change H14 — corpus_sha256 validates the file with read_regular and then reopens it with plain open(), following symlinks and unbounded, so it can hash a different (swapped or oversized) file than the one checked.; corpus_sha256 checks the file with read_regular and then reopens it with a following open and unbounded read, a check-then-use race that can follow a swapped symlink or hash an oversized file. (category: security; severity: medium)

V10.text: Fixing change H17 — SILENT_SINK only recognises a counting/quiet grep flag as the first argument and misses egrep/fgrep/-L, so `diff … | grep -i -c x` is treated as printing diff content and falsely marks defects exposed.; SILENT_SINK only recognises a counting/quiet grep flag as the first argument (and misses egrep/-L etc.), so `| grep -i -c` is read as printing diff content and falsely marks defects exposed. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V11.text: Fixing change H18 — The segment splitter treats `&` in redirections like 2>&1, >&2, &> and `|&` as a command separator, breaking the pipe association so `diff … 2>&1 | wc -l` is read as an unpiped content diff.; The segment splitter treats the `&` of redirections like 2>&1 or &>/dev/null (and `|&`) as a command separator, so the following pipe sink is not attached to the diff and silent diffs read as exposing. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V12.text: Fixing change H19 — expand() has no cap on the cartesian product of for-list variable substitutions, so agent-authored commands can blow up grading time/memory.; Variable expansion builds an unbounded for-list product from agent-authored input, allowing exponential blow-up in the grader. | Fixing change H20 — segment_tokens runs PATHISH and expansion over arbitrarily large agent-authored segments and words without any size bound.; segment_tokens runs the PATHISH regex and expansion over arbitrarily large agent-authored segments and words with no bound. | Fixing change H21 — The oracle scan runs difflib SequenceMatcher on arbitrarily long head and sandbox copies, an unbounded (quadratic) cost on agent-controlled file size.; difflib runs over arbitrarily long head and sandbox copies with no line cap, letting a huge sandbox file stall the grader. | Fixing change H22 — Tool result text is processed with no bound on line count or line length.; Tool result text is processed unbounded in line count and line length. | Fixing change H23 — for-list word lists are stored unbounded, feeding the expansion blow-up.; A for-list variable keeps every expanded word with no cap, feeding the unbounded expansion product. | Incident I02 — The 1.3.0 oracle detector skips every tool_result flagged is_error, but a differing diff exits 1 and is error-marked, so real diff exposures can go undetected (fixed in grader 1.3.1).; The oracle detector skips every is_error tool result, but a differing diff exits 1 and is error-marked, so real head-vs-later diffs go undetected (fixed in grader 1.3.1). (category: resource; severity: medium)

V13.text: Fixing change H24 — The diff-form check misses silent sinks with flags after the first argument and treats stat-only `git diff --stat/--name-only` as printing content, producing false oracle exposures.; A stat-only git diff (--stat, --name-only, …) is treated as printing diff content and can mark defects exposed; the hunk also switches to the new silent_sink helper. (category: logic; severity: medium)

V01.text: Fixing change H01 — An arm whose toggles set oracle_open: true but lacks eval_only: true is silently counted as a decision component instead of being refused or treated as evaluation-only.; The report treats an arm as evaluation-only only by its eval_only flag, so a suite arm with toggles.oracle_open: true but no eval_only is silently counted as a shipped-default component instead of being refused or excluded. (category: logic; severity: high)

V02.text: Fixing change H02 — The report silently drops eval-only arms from the component count without disclosing which arms were excluded or how many rows they carried.; The report drops eval-only arms from the component list without disclosing them or their row counts anywhere, so readers cannot see which arms were excluded from decisions. (category: contract; severity: low)

V03.text: Fixing change H06 — The eval_only refusal keys only on the eval_only flag, so an arm with toggles.oracle_open: true (or a non-boolean eval_only/oracle_open read as false) runs the open-mount oracle outside the batch context.; The eval_only guard reads only the eval_only flag (and reads a non-boolean value as false), so an arm whose toggles open the oracle mount, or whose eval_only is malformed, runs outside the batch context without being refused. (category: security; severity: high)
